newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss balloon cutting short world bid-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Swiss balloon cutting short world bid-spokesman.

text.p: A two-man balloon built to make the first-ever round-the-world flight will come down in the Mediterranean on Sunday only six hours after it took off from the Swiss Alps, an official spokesman said.

He told Reuters the Breitling Orbiter would hit water around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) off France after developing problems on board. The crew, Swiss Bertrand Piccard and Belgian Wim Verstraeten, were well, he added.

Speaking by telephone from the control centre for the flight at Geneva's Cointrin airport, the spokesman said helicopters would be on hand to pick up the pair from their bright yellow capsule. He could give no details of the problems.
"But they are both fine. It will make a soft touchdown in the sea," he added.

The helium-filled Orbiter took off from the mountain resort of Chateau d'Oex just before 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) but instead of taking course over Mont Blanc and down across Italy it drifted south-westwards over southern France.

Soon after mid-day, as skies across the region cleared after days of thick cloud, it was over the city of Orange with Piccard, from a famous family of balloonists, and Verstraeten, who runs his own ballooning company, reporting "problems on board."
